proposal: The Mandate says the national security adviser should reorganize the NSC by presidential directive, eliminate directorates not aligned with the President's agenda, staff most directorates with aligned political appointees and trusted career officials, return nonessential detailees on the first day, merge the NSC and Homeland Security Council (HSC) staffs, incorporate the Office of the National Cyber Director, hold and adjudicate security clearances inside the NSC, and give the NSC its own counsel without dual-hatted staff. It also calls for a strong, empowered NSC that can drive the bureaucracy.
remaining: Incorporation of the Office of the National Cyber Director into the NSC staff (the office remains a separate official in 2026 presidential documents)
A separate NSC counsel without dual-hatted staff (NSPM-1 keeps a deputy White House counsel who also advises the national security adviser; whether this meets the Mandate is an interpretation)
Evidence that the NSC holds and adjudicates its own security clearances (not found)
White House and OMB review of the National Defense Strategy and other formal strategies through the NSC (not examined)
A fully staffed, empowered NSC that drives the bureaucracy, which 2026 commentary says the reduced NSC does not currently do

status_summary: As of 2026-10-07 the NSC has been reorganized by presidential memorandum and personnel actions, but only some of the Mandate's elements are in place. NSPM-1 (2025-01-20) lets the NSC meet as the Homeland Security Council on topics agreed in advance and puts one staff and one Executive Secretary over both, a staff consolidation of the kind the Mandate describes. In April 2025 several NSC staff were fired, and on 2025-05-23 AP reported an overhaul of a staff of roughly 395 in which about 90 to 95 detailed experts were removed and free to return to their home agencies, with the staff expected to be significantly reduced; CBS reported about 20 staff placed on administrative leave and the communications team dissolved. Neither report gave a post-cut headcount. The National Cyber Director still appears as a separate report recipient alongside the national security adviser in EO 14413 (signed 2026-06-22, published 2026-06-25 at 91 FR 38487), and NSPM-1 gives one official both the Deputy Counsel to the President for National Security Affairs and Legal Counsel to the National Security Advisor titles. The Mandate also asks for a strong, empowered NSC; a July 2026 commentary by a former NSC deputy executive secretary says the NSC lost staff, expertise and responsibilities and that interagency meetings slowed, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio still also serves as national security adviser, so the outcome differs from that goal.

timeline.event: NSPM-1 reorganizes the NSC system: the NSC meets as the Homeland Security Council on topics agreed in advance by the National Security Advisor and the Homeland Security Advisor, one NSC staff under a single Executive Secretary serves both, and policy coordination committees are chaired by NSC staff. It does not mention the Office of the National Cyber Director or detailees, and it names the Deputy Counsel to the President for National Security Affairs, who is also legal counsel to the national security adviser, as a regular invitee.
CBS later reported that at least six NSC staffers were fired in early April 2025 after the President received outside opposition research on staffers (month known only; first of month used).
National Security Adviser Mike Waltz and deputy Alex Wong are reported to be leaving; Secretary of State Marco Rubio becomes interim national security adviser while remaining Secretary of State.

AP reports an overhaul of the NSC: staff of roughly 395 before the changes (about 180 support staff), with about 90 to 95 detailed experts removed and free to return to their home agencies, and the staff expected to be significantly reduced. CBS reports about 20 staffers placed on administrative leave, the communications team dissolved, and Vance aide Andy Baker and deputy chief of staff Robert Gabriel named deputies at the NSC. Neither report gives a post-cut headcount.

A Financial Times report, summarized on Wikipedia, says dozens of foreign policy and national security staff were removed and the NSC-led policy process had been sharply reduced (article not read directly).

EO 14413, Ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation (published 2026-06-25 at 91 FR 38487), routes reports on the national security implications of commercial quantum computers to the President through the science and technology assistant, the national security adviser and the National Cyber Director as separate officials, so the cyber director's office still operates alongside, not inside, the NSC staff structure (inference from the reporting chain).

The July-August 2026 Foreign Service Journal carries a commentary by a former NSC deputy executive secretary saying the NSC has shrunk in staff, expertise and responsibilities, the interagency meeting schedule has slowed, and Rubio still holds both posts (month known only; first of month used). Senior administration officials dismissed concerns, per the article.

title: Realign NSC staff to presidential priorities and fold in HSC and cyber functions
uncertainties: Staff figures differ by outlet (about 350 versus about 395 before the cuts) and no post-cut headcount was published in the articles read. The 2026 assessment of a weakened NSC comes from one commentary by a former NSC official, not from staffing data. The cyber office finding is an inference from the reporting chain in EO 14413 (Section 10(c) routes reports through the science and technology assistant, the national security adviser and the National Cyber Director as separate officials), not from a document about NSC structure; an earlier reference to a second document published the same day was not confirmed. Whether the NSC adjudicates its own clearances, whether a separate counsel was created, and whether directorates were formally eliminated were not found. A Federal Register search of presidential documents for NSC organization found only NSPM-1 being cited by a 2025-04-15 order. The Financial Times claim is second-hand from Wikipedia. Searches run: two web searches on NSC downsizing and 2026 NSC structure plus Federal Register queries for 'National Cyber Director' and NSC organization. Re-check on 2026-10-15: a Federal Register API search of presidential documents mentioning the National Security Council from 2026-10-01 returned none, and one web search for a new NSPM or NSC reorganization surfaced only 2017 and 2025 items; another search on folding the HSC into the NSC found only older commentary. NSPM-1's single-staff provision remains the only formal HSC step found.
